content.text: Xiaotang, the shelf is finished. I built it over the weekend using some old wooden boards. It has four tiers, each with a guardrail to keep things from falling off. I also applied some wood wax oil, so it should last through the summer. What do you think?

Wow, Yifan, this shelf looks really sturdy! You're so handy—you got it done so quickly. I'll go find a spot by the entrance of the building unit to set it up and print out the instructions to put next to it.
Okay, I also created an online shared spreadsheet to make it easier for everyone to register. The issue of Aunt Zhang's surplus vegetables you mentioned earlier can be piloted using this first.

Great! I'll immediately initiate a proposal in the community group and invite Aunt Zhang and others to be the first batch of 'distributors.' The registration system you designed earlier is very practical; it will help track usage and avoid waste.

Well, make the most of everything. After you set up the shelf, remember to take a photo and share it in the group chat so everyone knows its location. I’ll regularly check the table data to analyze peak usage times for both placement and retrieval, which will help optimize the rules.

No problem! I'll get right on it. You mentioned considering the freshness containers and the timing for distribution. Let's wait a few days after the pilot program starts to see the feedback before making a decision. For mutual aid and sharing, let's start with vegetables.

Yes, technological democracy and efficiency optimization. You’re in charge of organizing and promoting, while I handle the technology and setup, just like our previous division of labor. Let’s keep each other updated on any progress.

Okay! I've already set up the shelf in the right corner at the entrance of the building unit, sheltered from the wind and sun. The instructions are also posted, simple and clear. The response in the group chat has been positive. Aunt Zhang said she'll put some tomatoes and cucumbers there this afternoon.

The efficiency is quite high. I just looked at the spreadsheet, and there are already a few entries, like Aunt Zhang adding five tomatoes. It seems everyone is quite proactive. I suggest we observe for a while initially and not rush to change the rules.

Yifan, look at this information board next to the parcel locker. I've created a more detailed guide based on it and posted it next to the shelf. It includes instructions on how to register, suggested pickup times, and more, making everything clearer.

Good, practicality is key. The table data shows that the peak time for drop-offs is in the evening, while pick-ups mostly occur in the morning. This is likely because people drop off items after work and pick them up before heading to work. We could consider adjusting the instructions to encourage off-peak usage.

That makes sense! I'll update the guidelines. Also, Aunt Zhang mentioned that vegetables tend to dry out when placed on the shelf. Regarding the airtight containers you mentioned earlier, should we add a few more?

Sure, but let's not take too many for now to avoid waste. I'll find some old boxes to repurpose and bring them over this weekend. Being frugal and practical means making the most of what we have. According to the list, popular items are tomatoes and leafy greens, and airtight containers might be more useful for the latter.

Yifan, the pilot operation has been running for two days now. The shelves are well-stocked with a variety of vegetables and fruits, including tomatoes, cucumbers, and carrots. Everyone is highly engaged, and I shared some photos in the group to encourage them.

Noted, the human touch is truly heartwarming. The table analysis shows that the usage rate exceeds 80%, with minimal waste. Your organization and promotion efforts have been instrumental. We can now start discussing long-term rules, such as whether to set fixed distribution times.

Thank you! I think we could try releasing them on Wednesday and Saturday afternoons each week, while allowing free access at other times to avoid accumulation. Your logic is clear—could you help optimize it further?

Good idea, mild minimalism—the simpler the rules, the better. I'll update the table and instructions, and make adjustments when placing the fresh-keeping boxes this weekend. This collaboration has been very smooth, from idea to physical implementation, and the sense of community belonging has been strengthened.

Yes, a warm heart combined with practical skills has achieved mutual assistance, sharing, and making the most of resources. Keep observing and providing feedback, and communicate promptly if there are any issues. Thank you for your hard work, Yifan!

You're welcome, self-sufficiency, technological democracy. Don't worry too much or overwork yourself; just check in periodically. Sharing a bit about the smooth trial run helps lay a solid foundation for future projects.
Haha, I'll keep that in mind. Let's leave it at that for now and stay in touch! The shared vegetable basket went from an idea to reality, all thanks to you.
